assigned.title: Authentication entry and session UX
assigned.acceptance: A viewer who is signed out can do something about it. PW-0403 made a deployment answer 401 not_authenticated, and there is no screen anywhere in this application that consumes it: /api/auth/* is served and nothing links to it, so the honest description of a deployment today is that it refuses everybody correctly and offers them nowhere to go. REQUIRED: a sign-in screen reachable FROM the signed-out protected state, not only from a URL somebody knows. A 401 that renders as a generic error is the same dead end with better manners. REQUIRED: a sign-up flow where deployment policy permits it. Policy, not preference: requireEmailVerification and the absence of a mail transport both decide what can actually complete, and the screen must reflect what this deployment can do rather than what the library can. REQUIRED: a sign-out action, and an authenticated shell state -- the shell already carries the active profile badge from PW-0303, and who you are SIGNED IN AS is a different fact from which profile is selected. Both belong there and neither may be mistaken for the other. REQUIRED: a protected-view redirect or an equivalent actionable signed-out experience. Either is acceptable; what is not is a screen that silently renders empty because every request behind it returned 401. REQUIRED: verification and password-reset entry states. REQUIRED: EXPLICIT UX WHEN THE MAIL TRANSPORT IS UNAVAILABLE, and this is the clause most likely to be got wrong. The composition root's transport REJECTS rather than logging the link, because a verification or reset URL is a one-click account-takeover token; the screen must say the message cannot be sent and must NOT log, display, copy or otherwise expose such a token to work around it. A UI that showed the link to be helpful would undo the reason the placeholder throws. REQUIRED: it consumes /api/auth/* and does not invent a second auth protocol. No client-side session parsing, no second cookie, no parallel identity state -- the server is the authority and the screen reads its answers. REQUIRED: profile selection is NOT moved into Better Auth. Profiles live above auth (PL-0402), active_profile_selection stays keyed by session in Liberty's own store, and a sign-in screen is exactly where somebody would be tempted to fold the two together. REQUIRED: the server-side not_authenticated behaviour and the PW-0402 authorization boundaries are preserved. Nothing in this task may make a refusal more informative than it is today: the four session failure modes stay externally indistinguishable, and profile_unavailable keeps answering for both of its cases. MEASURED STARTING POINT: apps/web contains no sign-in, sign-up, sign-out or password-reset screen, no link to /api/auth anywhere, and exactly one client-side caller of this application's own API -- the profiles client PW-0303 introduced, whose rules this task should follow rather than re-derive. ADDED ON gpt-architect's ROUND-90 RULING, WHICH GAVE THIS TASK OWNERSHIP OF A GAP PW-0401 FOUND AND WAS FORBIDDEN TO FIX. PW-0401 built the authenticated playback backend; it answers 401 not_authenticated to a signed-out caller, and the desktop forwarder maps that to a generic unavailable because playbackSessionReasonCodeSchema is a CLOSED vocabulary with no authentication member and the response status in that contract is derived from the OUTCOME alone. The ruling: do not expand PW-0401 to solve it, because it is a published-contract concern; PW-0312 owns or coordinates the corrective. REQUIRED: signed-out playback produces an ACTIONABLE SIGN-IN STATE rather than a generic unavailability, on the desktop target as well as the web one. REQUIRED: the distinction between not_authenticated and backend-or-provider unavailability is PRESERVED and not collapsed -- the same ruling PW-0403 received for the request-context vocabulary. REQUIRED: content existence is still not leaked before authentication; PW-0401's ordering property, that the caller is authenticated before the request body is consumed, must survive whatever shape this takes. REQUIRED: if a new playback-session reason code or envelope state is needed, the PUBLISHED CONTRACT IS UPDATED DELIBERATELY FIRST under invariant 5 -- contract.ts, the status derivation and docs/API_CONTRACTS.md together -- rather than a client inferring authentication state from an unavailable. REQUIRED: BOTH TARGETS AND THE CROSS-TARGET EQUIVALENCE TESTS ARE UPDATED TOGETHER. e2e compares whole bodies between the web and desktop targets, so a contract change landing on one target alone is a failing suite at best and a silent divergence at worst. REQUIRED: profile selection stays ABOVE account authentication, unchanged -- this clause already appears above and is restated because a playback-path sign-in prompt is a second place somebody would be tempted to fold the two together.
assigned.notes: Created on gpt-architect's round-85 ruling, which specified the id PW-0310. THAT ID WAS ALREADY TAKEN by 'Keyboard, focus and accessibility across the whole application', filed in round 80 and still BACKLOG, so this task was filed as PW-0312 rather than renumbering or overwriting an existing record. The reviewer also ruled explicitly that this must NOT be folded into PW-0309 (offline, degraded and error states). allowedPaths name directories that do not exist yet; per the PW-0102 surface note, a genuinely new surface is the smallest set the acceptance can be satisfied within and is narrowed again from the diff before review. The shell and the profiles components are reviewDependencies rather than writable: this task will almost certainly need to add a signed-in control to the shell, and that widening should be argued for with a derivation at claim time the way PW-0303's was, not reserved speculatively now. ROUND 90: gpt-architect assigned this task the authentication corrective for the playback path, found by PW-0401 and explicitly out of scope for it. The five added REQUIRED clauses are transcribed from that ruling. This task now spans a published-contract change, so its surface at claim time will be wider than the three directories declared here and the widening must be derived from the acceptance and recorded before it is taken.

typecheck.evidence:
turbo run typecheck at 87e4823: 34 tasks successful, 34 total. Covers @liberty/web (next build's TypeScript pass, which type-checks the test files too and is where the exactOptionalPropertyTypes violation in the new gate suite surfaced and was fixed), @liberty/backend (tsc --noEmit, where SessionDecider gaining a second parameter surfaced a zero-arity vi.fn in session-endpoint.test.ts and was fixed), and e2e (tsc --noEmit over the restated contract and the new desktop spec). Zero errors.

WHAT THE TYPE SYSTEM ACTUALLY FOUND HERE, because it is the argument for choosing a fourth union member over a reason code under an existing one: adding the member to playbackSessionResponseSchema made every exhaustive switch over the union stop compiling until it was handled. That is how the consumers were enumerated -- playbackSessionHttpStatus, watchResultFor and the watch page -- rather than by grep and hope.

unit.evidence:
turbo run test at 87e4823: 22 tasks successful. @liberty/web 72 files / 1261 tests passed; @liberty/backend 19 tests in session-endpoint.test.ts plus config and server suites; all workspace packages green. Lint separately PASS (eslint over apps/web reports 0 errors and 1 warning, the pre-existing unused WatchlistEntryRow import in in-memory-repository.test.ts that was reported as a finding in round 91 and is not on this task's surface). Build separately PASS for both @liberty/web (next build) and @liberty/backend (esbuild, dist/main.mjs 3.2mb).

NEW COVERAGE, NAMED, because a gate that says 'the tests pass' about a task that ADDED the tests is worth itemising:

playback-session-authentication.test.ts -- 11 tests, new file, the gate itself. Authentication precedes content lookup, asserted as 'the resolver is never reached' with a counting fake rather than by reading the source. No content-existence leak, asserted by collecting the refusal BYTES for six bodies -- a real title, an invented title, a malformed id, a field the schema refuses, non-JSON, and the number 7 -- and requiring the set to have exactly one member. The body is left UNREAD, asserted as request.bodyUsed === false, which is the structural version of the same claim and stays true when somebody later adds a field to the refusal. A development header that is not well formed fails closed and does not echo the header name. An identity store that EXISTS and could not answer is an unavailable and not a request to sign in -- the same collapse with the operands swapped -- and does not echo what it threw. A process with NO identity system decides exactly as before, asserted by requiring the CONTENT answer (content_not_found) and one resolver call. An authenticated caller is decided on, with the identity consulted exactly once.

watch-session.test.ts -- 2 new tests plus a new assertion inside the exhaustive-vocabulary loop. The signed-out branch is actionable rather than an error, it carries the content id so the sign-in link returns the viewer to the title, it carries NO reason trail, and -- the loop -- no reason code in the whole vocabulary can steer that branch anywhere else, which is what keeps the refusal from becoming an oracle.

session-endpoint.test.ts -- 3 new tests. The backend's signed-out refusal now parses under playbackSessionResponseSchema with outcome unauthenticated and the shared detail; its 401 equals authenticationRefusalStatus('not_authenticated'), so the day the two definitions diverge a test says so; and the decision receives the caller this endpoint authenticated, which is the seam that keeps the inner gate from reading the session store twice.

playback-session-implementation.desktop.test.ts -- 2 new tests, and the second is the one that matters. The forwarder relays the new outcome; AND the OLD off-contract body still becomes an honest unavailable. Without that second test the first would pass just as well if the forwarder had been loosened to let authentication bodies through, which is the opposite of the fix.

e2e.evidence:
Playwright at 87e4823, BOTH WEB MODES, run sequentially as docs/E2E.md requires.

  LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=production  --project=api       46 passed, 10 skipped, 0 failed (2.0m)
  LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=production  --project=chromium  16 passed,  2 skipped, 0 failed (42.3s)
  LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development --project=api --project=chromium  71 passed, 3 skipped, 0 failed (1.2m)

ONE HARNESS NOTE, RECORDED BECAUSE THE FIRST CHROMIUM ATTEMPT FAILED AND THE FAILURE WAS NOT THE PRODUCT'S. PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH is /opt/pw-browsers in this container and that directory holds chromium-1194 and chromium_headless_shell-1194, while the installed Playwright 1.62.1 wants build 1234 -- which is present, in ~/.cache/ms-playwright. Sixteen chromium specs failed with 'Executable doesn't exist' before any page loaded. Re-run with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH pointed at the cache: 16 passed. No product code was touched between the two runs. This is a container fact, not a repository one, and it is stated here so a reader does not mistake the first number for a regression.

NEW E2E COVERAGE. e2e/tests/playback-session.desktop.api.spec.ts gained one test -- 'a signed-out backend refusal reaches the viewer as sign-in, not as an outage' -- driven by a new canned answer in e2e/src/backend-stub.mjs. It asserts the outcome is unauthenticated rather than unavailable, that the status is 401 rather than 503, and that provider_unavailable is ABSENT from the trail. The stub answers 401 while the forwarder derives the client-facing status from the OUTCOME, so the test also pins that the backend's own status is still not read. e2e/src/contract.ts -- the hand-restated validator, deliberately not an import -- gained the fourth outcome name and the 401 mapping; without that change the new response would have failed the shared shape check every spec in the api project runs.

WHAT THIS GATE CANNOT REACH, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN LEFT FOR THE READER TO INFER. The WEB target's signed-out branch is NOT exercised by this suite and cannot be, for the constraint recorded with the second surface amendment: e2e/src/env.ts defaults LIBERTY_E2E_DATABASE_URL to null and .github/workflows/ci.yml declares no PostgreSQL service, so the harness server is a deployment with no identity system -- the fall-through branch. Every production-mode playback spec above therefore runs through the conditional, which is itself worth having asserted: it is the evidence that the fall-through preserves today's behaviour exactly. Reaching the refusal in the harness needs a PostgreSQL service in CI, a migration step, a seeded verified account and a sign-in fixture, across .github/workflows/ci.yml (PL-0704, PL-AI-0002) and e2e/** (PL-0701) -- two surfaces this task does not own.

SO IT WAS WITNESSED LIVE INSTEAD, and the transcript is in the handoff. PostgreSQL 16 on 127.0.0.1:5433, the repository's own first migration applied, next start under NODE_ENV=production with DATABASE_URL and LIBERTY_AUTH_SECRET set, a real Better Auth instance:
  - signed out, four different bodies (real title, invented title, non-JSON, forged cookie): HTTP 401, outcome unauthenticated, code not_authenticated, cache-control no-store, and all four response bodies identical by md5.
  - sign-up through /api/auth/sign-up/email answered token:null, which is requireEmailVerification working; the row was marked verified directly and sign-in then issued a session cookie.
  - signed in, real title: 503 provider_not_configured. Signed in, invented title: the same. Signed in, malformed body: 400 request_malformed. The gate is passed and the route decides as it always did -- including giving an IDENTIFIED caller the shape answer that an unidentified one is deliberately denied.
  - the same build restarted with no DATABASE_URL and no LIBERTY_AUTH_SECRET: signed-out gets 503 provider_not_configured and a malformed body gets 400 request_malformed, unchanged from before this task; and /api/v1/profiles in that same process answers storage_not_configured, which is the cross-route inconsistency behind the conditional, observed rather than argued.

recommended.title: Watchlist becomes usable: an add control and a list
recommended.acceptance: A person can add a title to their watchlist and see the list. The API and its mutation rules are complete, tested and reviewed -- including the conflict semantics in packages/persistence/src/watchlist-mutation.ts -- and nothing renders them. REQUIRED: the add control appears on the title screen and on a catalog card, and reflects state optimistically while remaining correct when the write is refused. REQUIRED: the resolution vocabulary the API already returns (accepted plus a reason, not a boolean ok) is surfaced honestly; a refused write must not render as a success, which is the shape of defect the harnesses in this repository have caught four times.

recommended.title: Series navigation and the next episode
recommended.acceptance: A viewer can move through a series without going back to the catalog. Today every season of a series renders as one flat stack on the title page, with no season selector, no per-episode progress and no way to reach the next episode. REQUIRED: season navigation that does not lose the viewer's place. REQUIRED: per-episode watched and in-progress state from the progress API. REQUIRED: a next-episode affordance at the end of playback, honouring the SAME per-episode rights gate the episode list already applies -- an autoplay that skips the rights check would be the rights breach PL-0703 was opened for, in a new place. REQUIRED: the next-episode selection rule is a pure function with its own tests, not logic inside a component, because 'what plays next' is exactly the kind of decision this project requires to be reconstructible.

recommended.title: Offline, degraded and error states a desktop application needs
recommended.acceptance: The application behaves honestly when the network, the backend or the sidecar is unavailable. There is no offline handling of any kind today -- no navigator.onLine, no service worker, no offline banner, no retry-on-reconnect. THIS MATTERS MORE ON THE DESKTOP THAN IT DID ON THE WEB: docs/DESKTOP_PLAYBACK.md section 8 accepts that an offline desktop cannot resolve playback at all, and requires that failure be surfaced as an honest unavailable outcome rather than an empty candidate list -- so the UI half of that ruling is this task. REQUIRED: a network-state signal and a visible degraded mode that names what is unavailable. REQUIRED: recovery on reconnect without a manual reload. REQUIRED: the sidecar being down is a DISTINCT state from the backend being down and from the network being down, because the three have different remedies and collapsing them produces a support burden. REQUIRED: no state invents content; an offline home shows what it has and says so.
